outlook.statement: Quality Department will focus on continuous improvement by migrating the QMS to the CMMI version 3.0 framework and integrating AI-driven productivity enhancement tools.
Through off-shore leverage, Mindteck is seeking to increase exports and develop new markets through subsidiaries.

Under the reference forecast, global growth is projected to be 3.1 percent in 2026 and 3.2 percent in 2027, slower than its recent pace of about 3.4 percent in 2024–25, and to settle at about that rate in the medium term, slower than its historical (2000–19) average of 3.7 percent. Global headline inflation is expected to increase to 4.4 percent in 2026 and decline to 3.7 percent in 2027.
By 2030, it's estimated that AI agent-powered solutions could represent 60% of the total addressable software market—setting up a race between AI-native companies and incumbents.

Mindteck enters 2026 with a strong foundation in engineering, industry expertise, and client relationships. Best opportunities lie in AI-enabled, domain-driven, and outcome-focused solutions that help customers improve efficiency and innovation. Company will need to stay agile in technology investment, talent management, and risk control to sustain momentum.

Enterprise software market could potentially grow to USD 780 billion by 2030 (13% CAGR). 40% of enterprise applications will be integrated with task-specific AI agents by end of 2026, up from less than 5% today.
Global semiconductor sales expected to reach about USD 975 billion in 2026. 93% of industry leaders expect revenue growth in 2026.
Global medical devices market at roughly USD 605 billion in 2026, with longer-term growth toward about USD 1.03 trillion by 2034. CAGR estimates generally clustered around 5.9% to 6.2%.

Analytical instrument industry outlook for 2026 is positive and growth-oriented, with most forecasts pointing to mid-single-digit to high-single-digit CAGR. 2026 market roughly in the mid-USD 50 billion to low-USD 60 billion range.

Energy and utilities industry outlook for 2026 is challenging but constructive: demand rising fast from AI data centers and electrification. Electricity demand expected to grow by over 2% annually over next five years.
Business process outsourcing (BPO) projected to grow by over 9% annually through 2030. Total outsourcing market could reach around USD 800 billion by 2033.
The rapid evolution of digital technologies, including generative AI, data engineering, and advanced cloud ecosystems, continues to intensify demand for specialized IT skills in 2026.

risks: The Company has established a robust Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework designed to identify and assess business risks and opportunities. Through this comprehensive risk management process, the Company has identified several key risks and has developed mitigation strategies for each of them.
Geopolitical tensions could worsen, turning into the largest energy crisis in modern times.
Trade-related disputes could flare up.
Critical role of rare earth elements in global supply chains constitutes a particular point of friction.
Re-evaluation of profit expectations regarding AI or lowered expectations of viable markups could lead to decline in investment and abrupt correction in financial markets.
Larger fiscal deficits and increasing public debt could put pressure on long-term interest rates.
Erosion of institutions, including central bank independence and monetary policy credibility, could raise inflation expectations.
Scaling up of defence spending could boost economic activity in short term but bring inflationary pressures, weaken fiscal and external sustainability, and risk crowding out social spending.
Commodity price risk and foreign exchange risk due to changes in forex rate; the Board has taken a conscious decision not to have a formal hedging strategy for foreign exchange exposures.
Macroeconomic and budget volatility: IT spending sensitive to inflation, interest rate changes, tariff uncertainty, uneven global growth
Talent availability and retention: Competition for skilled talent in AI, cloud, cybersecurity, embedded systems, product engineering
Cybersecurity and digital exposure: AI-enabled attacks, deepfakes, ransomware, supply-chain vulnerabilities
Customer concentration and demand variability: Exposure to focused set of industries and customers creates risk of uneven revenue performance
Reputation and delivery risk: Delivery delays, quality concerns, security incidents, compliance lapses can affect client trust
Operating margin pressure: Clients demand more value, speed, lower cost; pressure on SG&A, utilization, pricing
Geopolitical and supply chain risks: Geopolitical tensions, export restrictions, supply disruptions, regional instability
Intense competition and rapid technology shifts: Global firms, specialized boutiques, AI-native entrants; accelerating technology cycles
AI and cloud governance: Responsible use, model accuracy, data privacy, regulatory compliance, cloud misconfiguration, access-control, resilience risks
Slowdown in discretionary spending: Organizations selective about new investments and outsourcing commitments
Workforce stability and well-being: Burnout, attrition, limited career progression
Highly competitive talent market sustaining pressure on attrition rates
